nodes_add.name: Jagat Singh
nodes_add.note: Retired chemistry professor; named by Sawan Singh in a will of 20 Mar 1948 per Beas records (installed 13 Apr 1948); Beas master 1948-1951; named Charan Singh by will of 22 Oct 1951.

nodes_add.name: Maulana Fazl Ahmad Khan
nodes_add.note: Naqshbandi-Mujaddidi shaykh of Raipur, Farrukhabad district; teacher of Lalaji. Birth 1838 or 1857 in different sources; per Dahnhardt (via EverybodyWiki) chose Lalaji as successor in 1896.

nodes_add.name: Chaturbhuj Sahay
nodes_add.note: Disciple of Lalaji; founded Ramashram Satsang at Etah in 1930, later based at Mathura.

nodes_add.name: Parthasarathi Rajagopalachari (Chariji)
nodes_add.note: Met Babuji 1964; president of Shri Ram Chandra Mission 1983-2014; his claim contested by Umeshchandra Saxena's side in litigation reaching the Supreme Court (2008). Named Kamlesh Patel successor Oct 2011.

nodes_add.name: Umeshchandra Saxena
nodes_add.note: Claimant to Babuji's succession and Mission presidency on the basis of a 1982 nomination (per the court record). Dates unknown.

nodes_add.name: Darshan Singh
nodes_add.note: Kirpal Singh's most widely recognised successor; led the Sawan Kirpal Ruhani Mission; b. 14 Sep 1921, d. 30 May 1989; succeeded by his son Rajinder Singh.

nodes_add.name: Ajaib Singh
nodes_add.note: Disciple of Kirpal Singh; founded Sant Bani Ashram in Rajasthan; recognised as successor by Sant Bani supporters in the US. Dates not verified.

glossary.def: Literally 'offering of the life-force'. In Sahaj Marg, the master's transmission of spiritual energy into the practitioner's heart.
'The natural path'. The heart-centred Raja Yoga method taught by Babuji and the Shri Ram Chandra Mission, now also called Heartfulness.
In Sufi practice, the shaykh's concentrated attention directed at a disciple's heart to transmit spiritual states.
One of the main Sufi orders, strong in India through its Mujaddidi branch, known for silent remembrance of God in the heart.
'Name'. In Sant Mat and Radhasoami teaching, the inner divine Word or sound current, also called Shabd.
Silent repetition of charged names, the first step of Sant Mat practice, followed by inner light (dhyan) and inner sound (bhajan).
'The path of the Father'. The movement around Ayya Vaikundar, centred on Kanyakumari and southern Tamil Nadu.
The principal scripture of Ayyavazhi, a long Tamil verse narrative that followers date to 1841.
A small Ayyavazhi place of worship and teaching, without idols and open to all castes.
An Ayyavazhi holy place; five major pathis centre on Swamithoppu.
The 'washing penance', a collective penance by Vaikundar's followers that tradition dates from 1840.

lalaji-babuji.mdx: Naqshbandi link and 1896 successor appointment rest on a secondary summary (EverybodyWiki citing Dahnhardt 2002, pp. 72-74) and on the Ramashram site; Dahnhardt was not read directly. The SRCM pages consulted (sahajmarg.org) do not name Fazl Ahmad Khan or Sufi training. Lalaji's birthplace Fatehgarh (Wikipedia, SRCM) vs Farrukhabad (Ramashram).

lalaji-babuji.mdx: Babuji's age at meeting Lalaji: 23 (Wikipedia, birth 30 Apr 1899, June 1922) vs 22 (sahajmarg.org); text gives no age. Babuji death 19 April 1983 (Wikipedia) vs 'April 1983' (SRCM). Chariji's birthplace Vayalur near Trichy (Wikipedia) vs near Chennai (sahajmarg.org); omitted from text.

lalaji-babuji.mdx: Supreme Court judgment (Civil Appeal 6619 of 2000, 29 April 2008) was read only through an Indian Kanoon summary and secondary case notes. The summaries conflict on the holding (one says dismissed and upheld the High Court; another says disposed with direction to decide the suit within six months, declining to decide the meaning of Sections 3(A) and 4). Text follows the second and quotes no judgment text. The date of Chariji's nomination is given as 1974 or 1994 in the court record and the SRCM gives no date. The final outcome of the Shahjahanpur suit after 2008 was not found. Grokipedia claims the Supreme Court upheld Chariji; the court record does not support this reading, and it was not used.

lalaji-babuji.mdx: partisan blogs (sahajmarglessons, srcmcultofindia, srcmshahjahanpur) could not be fetched and were not used. Umeshchandra Saxena's relation to Babuji (family or disciple) and dates are unknown. Dissent from Chariji's lineage to Daaji (2014 onward), any other splits, and the Heartfulness rename date were not found; text says only that the Mission now uses the name. The Bitter Winter article on the 2024 Paris administrative court ruling is by Massimo Introvigne, a writer who criticises MIVILUDES, and was not used in the text.

lalaji-babuji.mdx: the single quotation ('I became Thee and thou I') comes from sahajmarg.org/babuji-maharaj via fetch summary; attributed to Babuji describing his master's last message. Ten Maxims paraphrased from sahajmarg.org; authorship/date of the maxims not stated there. Wikipedia gives Commentary on the Ten Maxims as 1946.

lalaji-babuji.mdx: 'Ram Samadhi Ashram' (Thakur Ram Singh Bhati) listed on Wikipedia as a Lalaji lineage organisation; not otherwise checked. SRCM registration year: Wikipedia and SRCM say 1945; a case note (lawtext) says 'registered in 1995'; kept 1945.
lalaji-babuji.mdx: the node 'lalaji-babuji' combines two men; author may want to split it into lalaji and babuji nodes. If so, the sufi-orders -> lalaji-babuji edge should be replaced.

ayya-vaikundar.mdx: all life events rest on devotional texts and on English Wikipedia, which itself disagrees across articles: birth 1809 (Wikipedia, JETIR) vs 1820 (some Kerala blogs, not used); sea event 1 March, 3 March or 4-6 March 1833; arrest 1838 (Nov per Grokipedia) and release 6 or 26 March 1839; Wikipedia Ayyavazhi timeline is inconsistent on arrest. Penance length six vs about seven years. Death 2 or 3 June 1851. Akilam scribe Hari Gopalan Citar vs Arigopalan Citar and dictation 10 Dec 1841 vs 11 Dec 1840; Wikipedia Ayyavazhi says 1841.

ayya-vaikundar.mdx: the claim that London Missionary Society reports mention the imprisonment is from the English Wikipedia article and was not checked against the LMS record. 'Uplift of the lowly is dharmam' is from Wikipedia's summary of the movement's teaching, not from the Akilam text. Caldwell's 'largely negative view' is Wikipedia's wording; no Caldwell text was read. No scholarly book (e.g. Dick Kooiman, G. Patrick, Ponnu, Krishnanathan, Vivekanandan) was consulted directly.

ayya-vaikundar.mdx: no graph edges added. Ayyavazhi tradition mentions 'Thycaud Ayya' advising on Vaikundar's release (Wikipedia timeline) and popular accounts link Vaikundar with Chattampi Swamikal and Narayana Guru; none verified. Author to decide whether to add edges (existing node thycaud-ayyavu is a Tamil-born yogi, 1814-1909) once a source is found.

ayya-vaikundar.mdx: the 'mirror in place of an image' practice and the '7,000 Nizhal Thangals' count are from English Wikipedia's Ayyavazhi article. Adherent estimates (8 to 10 million) and census classification (counted as Hindu; about 243 self-identified in 2001 per Grokipedia) not used in text; Hindu/separate-religion debate is a candidate for a Critiques section if the entry is upgraded. Coordinates for Swamithoppu and Poovandanthoppu are approximate.
